problems.title: Model it

parts.prompt: Open the lock: a 4-wheel combination lock, one wheel turned by one notch per move, avoiding dead-ends. Nodes are…
options: the 10,000 combinations; edges are single-notch turns (8 per node)
the wheels; edges join adjacent wheels

problems.solution: The state space is implicit: 10⁴ combinations, each with 8 neighbours, and every move costs 1, so BFS.

problems.title: Islands
problems.solution: 5: the top-left 2 × 2 block, the pair at columns 4–5 of row 2, the single centre cell, the lone 1 at row 4 column 2, and the 1s at row 4 columns 4–5 (diagonals don't connect).

problems.title: Rotting

parts.prompt: Minutes until no fresh orange remains (or −1)?

problems.solution: The rot travels along the only path of fresh oranges; the farthest one, at the bottom right, is reached after 6 minutes.

problems.title: Why multi-source?

parts.prompt: One BFS per rotten orange, keeping each cell's minimum, costs about…

problems.solution: Seeding all sources at distance 0 is one BFS from a virtual super-source: O(cells).

problems.title: Enqueue or dequeue?
problems.statement: BFS on an open 100 × 100 grid with 8 neighbours per cell, marking cells visited only when dequeued.

options: A cell may be pushed by up to 8 neighbours before it is dequeued, multiplying the queue size

hints: When does a duplicate get in?
problems.solution: Distances stay correct, since BFS order still holds, but the queue holds duplicates, costing up to 8× the work and memory. Mark on enqueue.

problems.title: State design
problems.statement: Shortest path in a grid where you may remove at most k obstacles.

parts.prompt: Number of states for a 40 × 40 grid with k = 40?

hints: Two arrivals at the same cell with different budgets are different situations.
problems.solution: (r, c, used) with used ∈ [0, k]: 40 · 40 · 41 = 65,600 states. A visited set on (r, c) alone is wrong, because a later arrival with more budget left might succeed.

problems.title: Word ladder
problems.statement: begin = "hit", end = "cog", words = [hot, dot, dog, lot, log, cog].

parts.prompt: Answer (number of words in the sequence)?
Neighbour candidates generated per 3-letter word (26 letters per position, including the unchanged one)?

problems.solution: 5 words. Generating 3 × 26 = 78 candidate strings per word and checking a set beats comparing against every word when the list is large.

problems.title: Bidirectional BFS
problems.statement: A branching factor of 10 and a shortest distance of 6.

parts.prompt: Nodes explored by one-sided BFS, roughly (10^d)?

problems.solution: 10⁶ versus 2 × 10³: the frontiers meet in the middle. Always expand the smaller frontier.

problems.title: Border inward
problems.statement: Surrounded regions: flip every 'O' region not connected to the border into 'X'.

options: Flood-fill from the border 'O's to mark the safe cells, then flip everything else
From each 'O', search for the border

hints: Reverse the direction of the search.
problems.solution: One pass from the border marks every safe cell, so the whole thing is O(cells). Searching from each cell outward can repeat work O(cells) times.
